newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: HSBC HOPES FOR 20 PCT RETURN A YEAR IN ARGENTINA.
newsitem.headline: HSBC HOPES FOR 20 PCT RETURN A YEAR IN ARGENTINA.

text.p: HSBC hopes for a 20 percent return on equity for the $600-$700 million it will pay for Argentine financial services holding company Grupo Roberts.

"Our group as a whole is currently recording returns in excess of 20 percent per annum on equity," Keith Whitson, the chief executive of Midland Bank and chairman of HSBC's Latin American unit, told a press conference in Buenos Aires Friday.
"That is an indication of the sort of level of return we will eventually be able to receive in Argentina," he said. Nevertheless, he added that "a lot, of course, will depend on external conditions."

HSBC Holdings Plc, considered the world's largest financial services group, announced in May the purchase of Grupo Roberts, its latest deal in Latin America, where it also has interests in Brazil, Mexico, Chile and Peru.
Whitson said HSBC regards Latin America and Asia as the two areas of the world likely to see the most impressive growth in the foreseeable future.
In 1992, it acquired Midland Bank in what was at the time the world's largest single banking merger.

"We said at that particular time that it would probably take us approximately four years to digest the Midland acquisition," Whitson said. "That has gone very succesfully and about the middle of last year we started to look towards Latin America more seriously."
Whitson said Argentina's Central Bank gave HSBC Thursday formal approval for the acquisition of Roberts. He expects it to be signed within the next few days.

He also said that HSBC has concluded a transaction in Brazil to buy 100 percent of Bamerindus, the country's fourth largest bank, and was giving the final touches to buy slightly less than 20 percent of Mexico's Grupo Financiero Serfin.

Whitson said the Bamerindus acquisition was a major deal, but quite different from the Grupo Roberts takeover, as the Brazilian bank had experience major difficulties that led to intervention by the central bank.

"Opportunities don't always come along when one would like them too, but in this particular case we believe that we have been extremely fortunate to be able to expand in Brazil and Argentina" over a short period of time.
Whitson said Grupo Roberts' bank, Banco Roberts, was "first class" with good management.
Enrique Ruete, President of Grupo Roberts executive committee, will assume the chairmanship of Grupo Roberts, Whitson said. Michael Smith becomes executive director.
Whitson said he hoped other senior directors and managers of Grupo Roberts would continue to work with HSBC.
On Monday, HSBC announced record first half profits of 2.6 billion stg, 13 percent higher than in the same period year ago, Whitson said.
On Thursday, Banco Roberts announced a yearly net gain of $28 million, net worth of $283.7 million and retained earnings of $61.4 million.
